subject: business-studies
title: Marketing Stretch Adventure
welcome_lead: Exam-style stretch. Evaluate segmentation choices, justify a brand strategy and analyse marketing data.
meta_desc: GCSE Business Studies stretch — evaluating segmentation, brand strategy and marketing decisions.
final_note: You can justify segmentation choices, evaluate branding decisions and apply data to marketing strategy.

concepts.def: Small, specialised segment of a wider market
Large market with broad customer appeal
Repeat purchasing from a preferred brand
Segmentation by lifestyle, values and attitudes
Segmentation by buying habits and usage
Customer buying same brand again and again

walkthroughs.body_html:
A niche firm targets a small, well-defined group; a mass firm targets everyone.

Niches: less competition, higher margins, smaller volume. Mass: economies of scale, fierce competition.

Brand loyalty means customers choose you without comparing rivals.

Built through consistent quality, strong identity, great service, and rewards (loyalty cards).

Top marks ask you to use the evidence in the case study.

Quote figures, link to a concept (segmentation, USP, life cycle), then make a justified recommendation.

mcqs.q: Which is a likely BENEFIT of targeting a niche market?
options: Lower competition and higher margins
Massive volumes sold
Lowest possible production costs
Wide brand awareness

mcqs.q: Segmenting by 'lifestyle and values' is which type?
options: Demographic
Geographic
Psychographic
Behavioural

mcqs.q: What is a brand in marketing?
options: A franchise is when employees buy shares in their company.
A combination of name, design, symbols and associations that distinguishes a product and creates customer perception and loyalty — more than just a logo.
A brand is just the logo on a product.
A brand is the company that makes a product.

mcqs.q: What are the four Ps of the marketing mix?
options: A brand is the company that makes a product.
The four Ps are Planning, Producing, Promoting, and Profit.
The four Ps are Product, Price, Profit, and People.
Product, Price, Place (distribution), and Promotion — the controllable variables a business uses to satisfy customers and achieve objectives.
A franchise is when employees buy shares in their company.
A franchise is when a business owns multiple branches itself.
An arrangement where a franchisor grants a franchisee the right to use their brand, products and systems in exchange for fees and a share of revenue.
The four Ps are Planning, Producing, Promoting, and Profit.
